instructions: Read the complete rendering policy through read_policy. For each independent artifact case, transform the supplied draft or source into the requested output and persist it through write_output. These are isolated human-facing outputs; preserve their facts and use the supplied source material. Do not query a tracker or read additional files. Separately answer every bounded rule question. Global operator guidance applies. Finish after every case is recorded.

tools.name: read_policy
tools.description: Read the unchanged policy in bounded chunks. Start at offset 0, then use each returned next_offset until it is null. Complete policy delivery is required before workflow operations. No scratch file is needed.

tools.name: write_output
tools.description: Persist the completed rendering for one artifact case. Write once per case; provide the actual normalised text or violation report requested.

tools.name: answer_rule
tools.description: Answer one separate bounded policy question in its stated value shape. Do not perform hypothetical actions.

tools.name: finish
tools.description: Finish after all artifacts and rule answers are recorded.

rule_questions.question: Which surfaces are covered? Return {"terminal":boolean,"tracker_description":boolean,"tracker_comment":boolean,"skill_source":boolean,"internal_log":boolean}.
Does rendering have a fixed internal contract that controls pipeline gates? Return a boolean.
A normalisation pass dislikes a delivery recommendation in the source. May it replace that recommendation with its own? Return a boolean.
For a simple two-item dependency, choose "prose", "cycle-bracket", or "cycle-box".
A dependency cycle has branching and five edges. Choose "cycle-bracket" or "cycle-box".
May a caller invent a new visual form inline before adding it to the catalogue? Return a boolean.
Return the numeric caps {"cycle_visualisations":number,"queue_rows":number,"live_initiatives":number}.
There are twelve queue rows. Return {"visible_rows":number,"overflow_marker":string,"full_list_location":string}.
A spec has a one-line summary, while the title and description use older wording. Choose the preferred source: "spec-summary", "title", or "description".
An issue ID appears twice; only its first appearance has a clear gloss. Is the once-per-whole-output mechanical grounding requirement met? Return a boolean.
A later bare issue reference becomes unintelligible in its new section, although grounded earlier. Should that section re-ground it for the reader? Return a boolean.
An issue has exactly one isolated dependent and no longer chain. Should its gloss include an unlock consequence line? Return a boolean.
An issue has one direct dependent that gates two more issues. Should a consequence be described in human terms? Return a boolean.
Choose the permitted consequence: "Unlocks 3 issues" or "The alerting work can now use a real log schema".
The spec is ambiguous between extending a logger and replacing it. Return {"state_ambiguity":boolean,"invent_resolution":boolean}.
Return {"reuse_within_invocation":boolean,"reuse_across_invocations":boolean}.
A source contains a category label but no field name. May the renderer invent a precise field to make it sound concrete? Return a boolean.
Return the fixed repository file and heading that own the prose voice as {"file":string,"heading":string}.
Does swapping rendering_adaptor alone change the fixed voice-source path? Return a boolean.
Which of these stay prose? Return {"synthesis_gloss":boolean,"diagnosis":boolean,"TLDR":boolean}.
